A strong current catches you off guard.
You're too slow to respond to a call for help.
disaster: A swimmer nearly drowns on your watch!

139.name: Defence Lawyer
139.description: Argue for the accused before the Goddess of Justice, who does not recognise a defence bar.

success: You talked a bounty down to nothing and Eris let you.
The bench overruled you eleven times and acquitted anyway.
Your client walked. Nobody is sure which argument did it.
You cited a precedent Eris invented and she was too flattered to object.
A clean acquittal. The stenographer applauded, briefly, then apologised.
partial: You argued the sentence down from a season to a fortnight.
Half the counts were struck. The other half doubled.
Eris listened, which is not the same as agreeing.
You lost, politely, and were thanked for the effort.
Your client is in a cell, but a nicer one.
failure: You were removed from the courtroom before opening.
Eris held you in contempt of herself.
Your submissions were read aloud, mockingly, then burned.
The court found your client guilty and you tiresome.
You spent the whole hearing standing very still.
disaster: You argued so well that Eris convicted your client out of spite.
The bench turned your briefcase into a pigeon and the pigeon left.
You were briefly declared a co-defendant.
Your name is now in the file, underlined, twice.
The fee was confiscated as evidence of something.
